title.narrative: Study visit Healthcare Rehabilitation Centers from in NL

description.narrative: The purpose of the project is to implement a study visit in the Netherlands (NL) on rehabilitation centers by representatives of the Ukrainian working group (WG) of the Ministry of Health (MoH) working on building code rehabilitation centers.This visit will enable that 11 members of the WG-MoH get practical understanding of the Dutch requirements for the gradation of different types of rehabilitation facilities and the rehabilitation methods that need to be considered in the building codes of Ukraine for these facilities. The visit will also facilitate the communication of the delegation with architects who have experience in the design of these type of specialized healthcare facilities and with Dutch rehabilitation experts in the fields of cardiology, orthopedics, neurology, pediatrics and pulmonology, covering the rehabilitation of civilians and military personnel after injuries as consequence of the ongoing war.

title.narrative: Increased impact of an existing PSD project

comment.narrative:
Life Science and Health (LSH) sector is one of the priorities of EKN-Kyiv in Ukraine. This project contributes to strengthening the Dutch government's commitment to PSD.
This project (PTM24UA01) study visit on rehabilitation centers from Ukraine to NL, complements and provides conceptual and technical input to project PCB24UA01 Healthcare Building Code rehabilitation that provides technical advice and support to the Ukrainian government and the members of the Working Group (WG) working on the development of the building code for rehabilitation centers in Ukraine.
Rehabilitation centers are at the core of the plans of the Ministries MOH and MTU of Ukraine as they are crucial for the short- and long-term economic recovery and the reconstruction of Ukraine in the context of the ongoing war. The project strengthens the technical quality of the State Building code of Ukraine in the chapter of rehabilitation centers. It is expected that as result of this visit, the Working Group will develop the basic framework for the development of the Building code on rehabilitation centers tailormade for the Ukrainian situation. This criteria was provided to the consultant of project PCB24UA01 who is developing the proposal for the building code on rehabilitation centers for Ukraine. This building code aims to provide the rules of the game to foster the involvement of private actors in the provision of rehabilitation services.
The minister of BHOS is the coordinating minister of the NL government for supporting Ukraine during the war and reconstruction. Three Public Private Platform (PPP) have been implemented in the Netherlands in the following sectors: Agri and Food, Water; and Life Science and Health. The platforms are part of coordination of private sector initiatives for the Ukraine. Ukraine is a so-called combi country, which implies that Dutch private sector investments and trade supported by BHOS should contribute to SDG 8 (“decent jobs”). This project enabled that 10 representatives of Ukrainian Working Group (WG) working on building code rehabilitation centers get practical understanding of the Dutch requirements for the gradation of different types of rehabilitation facilities; and the rehabilitation methods that need to be considered in the building codes of Ukraine for rehabilitation facilities. The following members of this group participated in the study visit:
1 Representing the Ministry of Communities, Territories and Infrastructure Development of Ukraine MTU 1 Representing The Ministry of Health (MOH): 3 Representing the State Emergency Service 2 Representing the institute for public health of the National Academy of Medical Sciences of Ukraine 1 Representative NGO 1 representative of local govwernment 1 Representative of private sector: architectural and engineering company
Key results: • The primary outcome of the project was to provide the Ukrainian delegation with a comprehensive understanding of how rehabilitation care is organized and delivered in the Netherlands. • The delegation had a visit to the Dutch Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sports in The Hague, where they received a general overview of the Dutch Health system and the Dutch policy and approach on rehabilitation centers. Furthermore, the delegation visited eight rehabilitation organizations: - Spomed, Capelle a/d IJssel (Physiotherapy clinic) - Rijndam Revalidatie, location Dordrecht (Rehabilitation centre children) - Radboud University Hospital, Nijmegen (Rehabilitation centre, Tertiary care) - Sint Maartenskliniek, Ubbergen (Rehabilitation centre, Tertiary care) - ZZG Herstelcentrum – Zorggroep, Groesbeek (Rehabilitation centre) - Atlent Children’s Expertise Centre, Den Bosch (Rehabilitation centre and primary school for disabled children and young-adults – 0 till 21 years) - Revalidatie Kliniek Tolbrug, Den Bosch (Rehabilitation centre) - Daan Theeuwes Centrum, Woerden (Rehabilitation centre)
